authoredSolutions.20: The sliding bar is the seat of a motional EMF: by \(\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}\) (bar moving left, \(\vec{B}\) into the page) it acts as a battery driving current through itself in one fixed sense. \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) sit on opposite sides of this common source, so the induced current circulates in opposite senses in the two loops — clockwise through \(R_1\) and anticlockwise through \(R_2\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.37: At \(273\text{-}278\ K\), aniline undergoes diazotisation with \(NaNO_2/HCl\) to give benzenediazonium chloride, \(C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-\) — the intermediate X. Warming this diazonium salt with water (\(H_2O,\ \Delta\)) hydrolyses it to phenol, the major product A. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.39: Antihistamines block the action of histamine. \(H_1\)-antagonists relieve allergy (antiallergic), while \(H_2\)-antagonists such as cimetidine and ranitidine suppress gastric acid secretion (antacid action). So their functions are antacid and antiallergic. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.41: First reaction: \(20\%\ H_3PO_4\) protonates the \(-OH\) of 1-methylcyclohexanol and acid-catalysed dehydration follows Saytzeff's rule, giving the more-substituted alkene 1-methylcyclohexene (A). Second reaction: the bulky base \((CH_3)_3CO^-K^+\) forces Hofmann elimination on 1-chloro-1-methylcyclohexane, giving the less-substituted alkene methylenecyclohexane (B). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.44: Both statements are true. The enol of acetylacetone is stabilised by intramolecular hydrogen bonding (a six-membered chelate ring) together with conjugation with the second carbonyl, so it exists to about \(15\%\); acetone's enol has no such intramolecular hydrogen bond and stays below \(0.1\%\). R is the correct explanation of A. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.66: \(A^2=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\); squaring repeatedly gives \(A^8=\begin{bmatrix} 128 & -128 \\ -128 & 128 \end{bmatrix}\). The system becomes \(128(x-y)=8\) and \(-128(x-y)=64\), i.e. \(x-y=\tfrac{1}{16}\) and \(x-y=-\tfrac12\) at once — a contradiction. So the system has no solution. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.69: \(g\) is differentiable on all of \(\mathbb{R}\) (at \(x=1\) both pieces give slope 3). \(f\) is smooth except at \(x=0\), where it jumps (\(0+2=2\) from the left, \(0\) from the right). So \(f(g(x))\) can fail to be differentiable only where \(g(x)=0\), i.e. \(x^3=0\Rightarrow x=0\); there \(f\circ g\) is even discontinuous. That is the only such point, so the count is 1. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.71: The base \(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}<1\), so \(\log_{1/\sqrt2}t\le 2\) reverses to \(t\ge(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2})^2=\tfrac12\). With \(r=|z|\): \(\frac{r+11}{(r-1)^2}\ge\tfrac12\Rightarrow 2r+22\ge r^2-2r+1\Rightarrow r^2-4r-21\le0\Rightarrow (r-7)(r+3)\le0\), so \(-3\le r\le 7\). The largest value of \(|z|\) is 7. Hence option (B).
